author: reek
body: Proves a control deck now closes games with an evasive win-condition. A control pilot rarely clears the should-attack pressure bar, so before this its Serra Angel sat back and the deck durdled to the turn limit. Now a creature the opponent cannot block attacks -- its damage gets through. It is not strictly free (declaring the attack still gambles the opponent has no instant-speed response, which is only certain when they are tapped out) but vigilance makes Serra Angel the smallest-downside case: it flies in AND stays untapped to block, never trading defence for offence, so flying the clock in is the right bet for a win-condition. The attack is only made when the threat is genuinely unblockable: against an opponent that has a flier to block with, the control pilot still holds back rather than trading its win-condition into a bad block.
